query: Which method can be used for oxidation resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Stationary friction processing can improve the oxidation resistance of equimolar AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys by refining the grain structure, thereby promoting the formation of a protective oxide scale.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy with coarse grains (~98 μm) that tend to form nonprotective spinel oxides during oxidation.
generation.intervention: Application of stationary friction processing (e.g., using a WC-cylindrical tool at high rotational speeds such as 1800 rpm for 5 minutes) to induce severe plastic deformation.
generation.conditions: Isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at elevated temperatures (850°C, 950°C, and 1050°C) for durations around 100 hours.
generation.structural_mediator: Ultrafine-grain microstructure (grain size reduced to submicron levels) with increased grain boundary density and enhanced surface free energy.
generation.mechanism: The refined grain structure facilitates rapid outward diffusion of chromium and aluminum ions, which in turn leads to the formation of a continuous, protective Cr2O3 and Al2O3 oxide layer instead of nonprotective spinels, thereby decelerating oxidation kinetics.
generation.predicted_outcome: Friction-processed samples will exhibit lower cumulative mass gain and reduced parabolic rate constants during oxidation compared to as-cast samples.
generation.baseline: As-cast alloy showing coarse grains, higher mass gain due to oxidation, and formation of nonprotective spinel oxides during exposure.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies under the specified oxidation temperatures (850–1050°C) and durations (around 100 hours); variations in alloy composition or processing conditions may lead to different outcomes.
generation.uncertainty: The exact quantitative improvement in oxidation resistance depends on optimization of processing parameters; further testing is required to determine the optimal processing conditions and to generalize these findings to other high-entropy alloy systems.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy samples: one set retained in the as-cast state and another set processed by stationary friction processing at 1800 rpm for 5 minutes. Subject both sets to isothermal oxidation at 850°C, 950°C, and 1050°C for 100 hours in laboratory air. Compare oxidation kinetics and oxide scale composition.
measurements: Grain size characterization via scanning electron microscopy (SEM)
Mass gain measurements using thermogravimetric analysis (TGA)
Phase identification of the oxide scale via X-ray diffraction (XRD) and electron microscopy
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the friction-processed samples do not show a statistically significant reduction in oxidation mass gain or if the protective Cr2O3/Al2O3 oxide scale is not predominant compared to the as-cast samples (i.e., if nonprotective spinels continue to dominate), then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: How does an ultrafine-grain microstructure, obtained via stationary friction processing, affect the oxidation behavior of AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy?. System: Equimolar AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy (HEA). Processing: Stationary friction processing (SFP) using a WC-cylindrical tool (12 mm diameter) at rotational speeds of 400 rpm and 1800 rpm for 5 min duration. Test conditions: Isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at 850, 950, and 1050 °C for 100 h. Findings: Grain size refined from 98 μm (as-cast) to 1 μm (SFP_400) and 0.43 μm (SFP_1800).; Phase transformation from BCC/B2 to FCC occurred, with 38% and 55% FCC fraction for SFP_400 and SFP_1800, respectively.; Surface free energy increased by 29.8% for SFP_400 and 35.2% for SFP_1800 compared to as-cast.; Oxidation kinetics decelerated by 12–20% for SFP_400 and 38–48% for SFP_1800 compared to as-cast.; Cumulative mass gain at 850 °C after 100 h was 0.33 mg/cm² (as-cast), 0.27 mg/cm² (SFP_400), and 0.17 mg/cm² (SFP_1800).; Parabolic rate constants (k_p) at 1050 °C were 23.2 × 10⁻¹³ g²·cm⁻⁴·s⁻¹ (as-cast), 18.4 × 10⁻¹³ (SFP_400), and 8.16 × 10⁻¹³ (SFP_1800).; Processed samples formed predominantly protective
